narrative.overview:
Paduna looks like a calm surface hiding real operational power underneath. Every screen — Owner dashboard, expense tracker, stock movement, reconciliation — carries genuine financial and material control (budgets, margin risk, cash ledger, over-budget approvals), but presents it the way modern iOS presents a bank balance: flat tonal layering, one confident dark surface for the number that matters, quiet grouped rows for everything else, and a single restrained terracotta accent reserved for what actually needs attention. Nothing shouts. A project team member checking material readiness one-handed at a job site, and an Owner scanning margin risk in 30 seconds from a phone, should both feel the same unhurried confidence — competence expressed through restraint, not decoration.

This is deliberately not a generic SaaS admin dashboard and not a dense accounting spreadsheet. It borrows iOS's clear grouping, confident typography, and disciplined motion, not its glass, gradients, or oversized chrome. The system draws its entire color vocabulary from a monochrome ink-and-canvas foundation plus exactly one accent family (terracotta), so status and priority read through intensity and position, never through a rainbow of category colors.

The same identity spans one responsive web application: the mobile composition supports field work, while desktop uses compact controls and contextual tables for comparison and review. Canonical routes and the existing web session serve every authenticated role within its domain permissions and project scope.
keyCharacteristics: Solid tonal layering (canvas → white owner surface → inset gray) doing the structural work, finished with a barely-perceptible resting lift on owning surfaces — never glass or heavy elevation
One monochrome ink primary, one terracotta accent family covering both focus and warning/critical
Compact but never cramped: hierarchy carries density, not shrunken type
Fully capsule-shaped controls (buttons, tabs, badges, inputs) contrasted with 28/20/16px-radius container surfaces
Motion is restrained and purposeful — spring-based, never decorative or continuous
One responsive workspace, with compact desktop density and the existing mobile composition sharing the same visual language

rules.name: The Planned RAP Review Rule
rules.body: AI RAP proposals keep project identity, row count, proposal estimate and budget condition in a compact `ProposalCardShell` with one contextual review action. Review begins with project identity at the section-title role (17px) beneath the sheet headline (24px), followed by the budget decision, Material allocation comparison and material rows in one stable `FormSheet`. Material rows use shared `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` on desktop and mobile. Identity and area/unit lead each row; the primary subtotal stays on the right on desktop and below context on mobile. Label Kebutuhan, Buffer and Harga with their units, then show stock/shortage and price-source context. One inline editor is active at a time beneath the row summary. “Ringkas” collapses the editor without applying corrections; controlled editor inputs remain mounted and inert while collapsed. Keep unit-cost source copy associated with the price `FormField` helper; area, quantity, buffer and unit estimate are editable, while material identity and unit stay fixed. Pass the concise budget summary through shared `desktopAsideSummary`; shared sheet chrome owns its desktop right-panel scroll and keeps protected actions outside it. Mobile keeps the summary above rows and actions in the sheet footer. Lead the budget summary with a status icon, a concise verdict and any over-allocation amount. Keep “RAP setelah usulan” and “Alokasi Material” as divided `FactRow` rows in one white `GroupedSurface`, with the same stacked reading order on mobile and in the narrow desktop aside, without a nested metric panel. Use the optional shared `wrapLabel` behavior for narrow fact labels and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values; other `FactRow` consumers retain their default label behavior. A plain `FormDisclosure` contains existing RAP, proposal addition, actual spend, pending review and financial remaining budget, with labels and amounts on opposite edges. Desktop places “Rincian budget” in a white `GroupedSurface` in the wide main column below the Material rows; the aside retains the concise budget verdict, primary plan/allocation facts and protected actions. Mobile keeps budget detail within the summary. Reuse the existing 16px horizontal disclosure wrapper with `FactRow inset={false}` for one inset owner. Disclosure expansion, pagination and local correction state survive resize. The verdict compares total planned RAP after the proposal (existing RAP plus proposal addition) against Material allocation; proposal edits leave actual spend, pending review and financial remaining budget unchanged. Local edits recalculate subtotals and budget impact immediately. “Terapkan koreksi” persists reviewed corrections before the separate “Simpan draft RAP” action; unapplied edits, validation errors and pending operations prevent saving. Shared dirty-form dismissal protects unapplied changes, and reopening restores applied corrections. Preserve five-row pagination on mobile and desktop, stable input DOM and draft/page state across resize. Shared review rows and `BottomSheet` aside-footer placement preserve their separate content and overlay responsibilities; other consumers retain their defaults. Applying corrections or saving a RAP draft is never presented as budget consumption, stock reservation or cash movement. Review opens at natural content height and grows with disclosures or editors, bounded by the viewport; a desktop aside measures its inner content independently. The shared sheet-header canvas scrim covers the actual header height before fading over 16px, keeping scrolled content from competing with the title without changing sheet geometry. The review collection owns one white `GroupedSurface`, matching the budget surface's 28px radius and `shadow-surface` depth on mobile and desktop; inline editors use an embedded `FormSection`. Mobile editors reuse the public stacked `FormField` layout with sentence-case labels above start-aligned regular-weight Manrope values, retaining the 16px editable-text floor and tabular digits. Desktop editors use the shared `FormSection contentClassName` inner two-column grid, with Area and unit price spanning its width; mobile keeps stacked fields. Kebutuhan and Buffer reuse `NumericInput` with associated unit helpers. Area uses the public wrapping `Textarea` and normal caret editing. The `MoneyInput` label names the price unit, with the currency prefix beside its input value; row numbers remain in accessible labels rather than repeating in the visual form. Notes stay in a secondary plain `FormDisclosure`.

rules.name: The Saved RAP Changes Review Rule
rules.body: Saved Draft RAP corrections keep project identity, edit/delete counts and the estimated RAP total after changes in a compact `ProposalCardShell`, with an action chosen by the Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. A small single-row correction without Material Master replacement or allocation risk exposes all changed fields in the chat card and saves directly; a small single-row deletion adds one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. Multiple rows, larger patches, Material Master changes and allocation risk retain a wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal. In that sheet, desktop uses `desktopFooterPlacement="aside"`: project identity and edit/delete counts lead the left pane above shared `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` grouped rows; the right aside receives grouped budget facts through shared `desktopAsideSummary`, with shared sheet chrome owning summary scrolling and protected actions. Mobile retains project identity, budget facts, divided material rows and a protected bottom footer. Retained desktop and mobile sheets keep material review rows in one white, 28px grouped owner with the same `shadow-surface` depth as the budget summary; inline rows reuse embedded `ReviewCollection` inside the chat card. Rows show identity, explicit change/delete status and primary subtotal before their visible contextual differences, without selection or inline editing controls. Lead the budget facts with an icon and concise Material allocation verdict, followed by before/after RAP totals and Material allocation as divided `FactRow` rows in one white `GroupedSurface`. Show the over-allocation amount only when present. Reuse `wrapLabel` and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for wrapping fact labels and complete, unwrapped rupiah values. Each material row keeps its name, area and unit beside explicit edit/delete status. Updates use shared stacked `ProposalDiffRow` comparisons for changed fields. Show changed identity, detail and source fields explicitly: name, unit, Material Master reference, specifications, internal note and stock/purchase/vendor source. Material Master references use the recognizable material name or “Tanpa Material Master” without exposing raw IDs; changed subtotals use the same labeled two-column stacked comparison on desktop and mobile; deletions retain the quantity and subtotal with concise copy explaining that only the RAP row is removed. Keep the immutable proposal review separate from the existing planned-RAP editor: corrections return through chat. Retained sheets paginate five rows per page on mobile and desktop, preserving the reviewed row anchor across resize. Explicit actions in the chat card, desktop aside or mobile footer save the reviewed changes, expose the contextual correction action and state the result. Any deletion opens one short shared destructive `ConfirmationDialog`, from the card or retained sheet, naming the deletion count and any companion updates before saving together. Stale or expired proposals prevent confirmation and offer a fresh proposal; pending operations prevent repeat submission. Material Master, stock and cash remain outside this operation. This pattern extends the existing cool canvas, white grouped surfaces, Manrope roles and shared compact controls without introducing new tokens or a separate visual world.

rules.name: The Package Planning Review Rule
rules.body: AI proposals for Draft Tukang and Subcon packages keep project identity, create/update counts, projected category plan totals and any allocation warning in a compact `ProposalCardShell`, with an action chosen by the Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. A small correction to one existing package, with the same vendor and no allocation risk, exposes complete before/after values in the chat card and saves directly. Package creation, template-based planning, vendor changes, larger patches, multiple packages or allocation risk retain a wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal using shared `desktopAsideSummary`: desktop places shared `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` grouped package rows on the left, with category budget panels and protected actions in the shared right aside; mobile keeps category panels above grouped package rows and actions in the bottom footer. Budget decisions lead with an icon and concise verdict, including the excess amount when present. Projected plan and category allocation remain the primary divided `FactRow` values; previous plan, actual spend, pending review and remaining financial budget stay in a plain `FormDisclosure`. Desktop places independently controlled “Rincian budget Tukang” and “Rincian budget Subcon” disclosures in one white `GroupedSurface` below the package rows, while primary category budget facts and protected actions remain in the aside. Mobile retains each disclosure inside its category summary. Reuse the existing 16px horizontal disclosure wrapper with `FactRow inset={false}` for one inset owner. Independent category disclosure states and pagination survive resize. Reuse wrapping fact labels and complete, unwrapped `MoneyValue` amounts. Package identity retains category, area, unit, create/update status and optional vendor context. Show quantity, unit cost, scope and any internal note with the manual/template price-source label; updates use stacked `ProposalDiffRow` comparisons for changed fields, and changed subtotals use labeled stacked comparisons on desktop and mobile. The primary package estimate sits on the right on desktop and below context on mobile. Read-only whole-batch proposals have no per-row selection or inline editing controls. Retained sheets use white `GroupedSurface` owners for category panels and package rows, with the established 28px radius and surface shadow; the shared aside retains its 16px shadow gutters. Inline package rows use embedded `ReviewCollection` inside the chat card. Retained sheets paginate five rows per page on mobile and desktop, preserving the reviewed row anchor and open review through resize. The stored proposal remains immutable in this review; corrections through chat produce a fresh complete proposal while retaining the packages the user still wants. Explicit saving from the card or retained sheet sends only the stored proposal identity and saves the reviewed creates/updates together as Draft packages. Stale or expired proposals block saving and expose the fresh-proposal action; pending operations prevent repeat submission. Readiness and finalization use their dedicated protected review; Edit Lagi and Draft deletion use the separate RAP lifecycle review. Package planning does not move stock or cash or change actual budget usage.

rules.name: The RAP Readiness and Finalization Review Rule
rules.body: AI readiness and finalization proposals keep project identity, the pending or saved business outcome, the business-decision count, known RAP plan total and any budget risk in a compact `ProposalCardShell`, with an action chosen by the Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. One readiness/status decision affecting one package, without budget risk, exposes its full before/after result in the chat card and saves directly. A single finalization decision without budget risk uses the card plus one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. Multiple steps/packages or budget risk retain a wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal using shared `desktopAsideSummary`: desktop places readiness facts and an ordered business-decision review in shared `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` grouped rows on the left, with overall budget facts and protected actions in the shared right aside. Mobile reads budget first, then readiness and divided decision/verification rows, with actions in the bottom footer. Decision titles and essential outcomes remain visible immediately; this immutable batch has no selection or editing controls. Chat and sheet headers describe the pending or saved outcome rather than stage arrows. Project value, internal cap and the known Material/Tukang/Subcon plan remain primary divided `FactRow` values. The status combines an icon with a concise verdict naming category overruns and any internal-cap risk; budget risk stays visible during the decision. A plain `FormDisclosure` holds allocations, applicable plans, actual spend, pending review and remaining amounts for all five expense categories, plus aggregate actual-based margin. For retained sheets, desktop places “Kategori & realisasi” in a white `GroupedSurface` in the wide main column below the reviewed decisions; the aside retains the concise budget verdict, primary project/cap/plan facts and protected actions. Mobile keeps this financial disclosure within the summary. Reuse the existing 16px horizontal disclosure wrapper with `FactRow inset={false}` for one inset owner. Controlled expansion and reviewed-page state survive resize. Reuse wrapping fact labels and complete, unwrapped `MoneyValue` amounts. Readiness facts identify Material completeness and the reviewed Tukang/Subcon package or explicit unused-scope decision. Decisions that mark packages Siap disclose the exact affected package names, scope, area, quantity/unit, total estimate and optional vendor in a plain `FormDisclosure`. “Yang akan disimpan” names the review of package readiness, explicit scope choices and final lock decisions. Count these business decisions without counting backend `ADVANCE` steps. Compress each consecutive advance group into one “Konfirmasi kesiapan RAP” verification row, naming exactly the checked parts; partial checks must not imply all parts were checked. Preserve decision/verification order and affected-package details, without exposing separate “Lanjut ke” wizard rows or inferring a skipped scope or silently marking packages Siap. Retained sheets paginate the displayed review rows five at a time on mobile and desktop; inline decisions reuse embedded `ReviewCollection` inside the chat card. Preserve review state through resize. Retained sheets reuse the established white, 28px `GroupedSurface` owners for budget, readiness and decisions, with shared sheet chrome retaining the 16px aside shadow gutters. The proposal is read-only; chat corrections request a fresh complete proposal and clarify unresolved package/scope choices. Only explicit user confirmation sends the stored proposal identity and commits the reviewed batch. Any finalization opens one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`, from the card or retained sheet, stating that RAP will be locked, later changes require revision and no stock or cash moves. Finalization is the terminal lock step. Stale or expired proposals disable confirmation and offer a fresh proposal; pending operations prevent repeat submission. This review changes only the explicitly reviewed statuses, scope and stages, without consuming budget or moving stock or cash.

rules.name: The RAP Lifecycle Review Rule
rules.body: AI proposals for new RAP revisions, Edit Lagi or deletion of Tukang/Subcon packages, and manual/library Material additions keep project identity, the action summary, affected-part count and plan total after the action in a compact `ProposalCardShell`, with an action chosen by the Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. A single package reopen exposes its before/after status in the chat card and saves directly; a single package deletion adds one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. New baseline revisions, Material additions and multi-package changes retain a wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal using shared `desktopAsideSummary` and `desktopFooterPlacement="aside"`: desktop places the reviewed parts in shared `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` grouped decision rows, while the right aside owns budget facts and protected actions. Mobile reads the same budget summary before plain divided semantic rows, exposing each part’s identity and full reviewed outcome, with actions in the bottom footer. The sheet opens at natural content height and grows with disclosures within the viewport. Budget and review content reuse white, 28px `GroupedSurface` owners, with embedded review collection content when an owner already exists. Decision identity, action/status changes and contextual detail remain visible; this read-only batch has no selection or inline editing controls. The sentence-case “Yang akan disimpan” heading sits outside the review owner. Revision reasons use left-aligned supporting prose inside their owning grouped surface. Lead the budget summary with an icon and concise allocation verdict, then the plan total after the action and internal cap as divided `FactRow` values. A plain `FormDisclosure` carries project value, allocations, known plans, actual spend, pending review and financial remaining budget for all five categories, plus actual-based margin. For lifecycle actions retaining a sheet on desktop, “Rincian budget” sits in a white `GroupedSurface` in the wide main column below the reviewed parts; the right aside retains the concise budget verdict, plan total, internal cap and protected actions. Mobile retains budget detail within the summary for every lifecycle action. Reuse the existing 16px horizontal disclosure wrapper with `FactRow inset={false}` so content has one inset owner. Controlled expansion survives mobile/desktop resize. Reuse `wrapLabel` and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for readable labels and complete, unwrapped rupiah amounts. Each part names its category and action, translated before/after status, scope or area/quantity context, estimate and applicable revision number. New revisions show the reason and the selected Material/package parts copied to Draft, while the locked baseline remains intact; the new draft requires review and finalization again. Edit Lagi returns a Siap package to Draft, and Draft deletion names the exact package removed. Material additions identify user estimates or Item & Price Library prices, including any override reason; a plain “Rincian isian” disclosure exposes required quantity, buffer, unit price, translated material source, specifications and internal notes. Retained sheets paginate five rows per page on mobile and desktop; inline package rows reuse embedded `ReviewCollection` inside the chat card. Preserve the reviewed anchor and open review through resize. The review is read-only; corrections through chat request a fresh proposal. Explicit whole-batch saving sends only the stored proposal identity. Any package deletion opens one short shared destructive `ConfirmationDialog`, from the card or retained sheet, naming the deletion count and companion changes before saving. Stale or expired proposals block saving and expose a fresh-proposal action; pending operations prevent repeat submission. Saved chat-card summaries use completed tense for Material additions and package reopen/delete counts. The inline action area or protected sheet footer preserves the action-specific saved outcome and next step: Material has been added to the RAP plan; a new revision requires review and finalization again after all parts are ready; reopened packages require correction and a new Siap decision; deletion confirms that the selected Draft packages were removed. Keep the stock/cash status visible after saving. These actions change internal plans and reviewed package status without moving stock or cash or changing actual budget usage.

rules.name: The AI RAB Draft Review Rule
rules.body: AI RAB draft proposals keep project identity, selected-row count and selling total in a compact `ProposalCardShell` with one contextual “Review RAB” action. One wide, natural-height `FormSheet` owns review, focus and dismissal. Desktop uses shared `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` grouped client rows, with concise selling-total/Draft facts and protected actions in the shared right aside. The primary subtotal stays on the right on desktop and below context on mobile; client identity, description, quantity/unit and labeled selling price remain readable before expansion. Mobile keeps summary facts above the divided rows. Inclusion uses the shared labeled `ChoiceRow` review presentation in the action row beside Edit at every width, leaving identity and financial context the full row width. One inline editor is active at a time, with shared stacked client fields and a desktop two-column inner grid supplied by `FormSection contentClassName`. Inputs remain mounted and inert while collapsed. RAB title and client notes use one grouped form. Client name, description, quantity and selling price are editable; the source unit stays read-only. Reuse `FormField`, `Textarea`, `NumericInput`, `MoneyInput`, `ChoiceRow` and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"`, retaining complete, unwrapped rupiah values. Shared modal canvas, white grouped owners, corners, motion, focus and dismissal remain authoritative. Paginate five rows at every width. A plain “Sumber yang digunakan” disclosure below the review follows the current page and identifies selected source names, business categories and revisions without exposing raw IDs. Selection and client corrections persist in the owned 30-day review draft with an applied revision and survive pagination, reopening and resize. Local changes recalculate selling totals immediately, block “Simpan draft RAB” and use the shared discard protection; discarding unapplied input preserves the last applied review. “Terapkan koreksi” persists selection and client corrections before the separate business save. Keep its disabled control mounted after successful application so it cannot become Save under the pointer. Conflicts offer the latest draft with discard protection; stale or expired proposals block saving and expose a fresh-proposal action, while pending operations prevent repeat submission. Explicit save sends the owned proposal identity and expected review revision, creating only the exact selected client rows without silently copying baseline manual rows or bundles; the approved RAB baseline remains intact. Confirmed title, notes and row fields render as static client content, and the protected action becomes “Buka RAB proyek” with a saved-result message. Confirmed rows keep enabled shared “Rincian” / “Ringkas” actions on mobile and desktop to reveal and collapse static client fields, including the selling price per unit; they have no inclusion selection controls. Saved Draft corrections, client bundles and approval/revision/Change Order decisions may continue through separate explicit workflow proposals or manual project actions; publication remains a manual project action. Only client identity, description, quantity, unit and selling prices enter RAB content; internal cost, margin, vendor information and internal notes stay outside it. Saving creates a Draft without changing stock, cash or project budget. After confirmation, the review collection and pagination show only the actually selected and saved subset; excluded proposal rows never appear as saved RAB contents, while the original choice count or context may remain in a historical summary.

rules.name: The AI Expense Batch Review Rule
rules.body: AI project expense batches reuse `ExpenseBatchCard` for 1–50 rows and the established RAP/RAB review grammar: a compact `ProposalCardShell` keeps project identity, ready/review/submitted counts, selected count and exact total readable, with its review action in the footer. One wide, content-sized `FormSheet` owns review with preserved dismissal. Desktop keeps reviewed rows in the left pane, with just the selected-row count and total submission amount as divided summary facts above protected actions in the shared right aside; mobile reads the same two-fact summary before rows and keeps bottom actions. Chat correction is one full-width secondary action below submission; project navigation sits with metadata discard below the review content, outside the protected commit area. Reuse white divided `ReviewCollection` / `ReviewItem` rows, five-row pagination at every width and shared labeled `ChoiceRow` review controls beside Edit, keeping selection distinct from validation and submitted status. Each row exposes category/material identity, complete nominal, quantity/unit and the explicit reviewed Material stock effect; supplied physical/reserved stock comparisons remain visible. The draft’s plain “Rincian budget” disclosure stays below reviewed rows at every width, showing the proposed category amount, allocation, current realization and pending review only with budget-view permission. Corrections use one active embedded `FormSection` editor with shared `FormField`, `Textarea`, `NumericInput`, `MoneyInput` and `AdaptiveSelect`, stacked fields on mobile and a two-column inner grid on desktop. Sentence-case labels lead regular-weight, start-aligned values; description, category and nominal span the desktop editor width. Material stock/RAP fields and Tukang/Subcon package fields follow their matching category. Optimistic choices remain immediately visible while one serialized queue saves selection metadata; browsing and further selection stay usable during synchronization, while submission waits for acknowledgement. Local corrections, selections and applied review revisions survive reload, reopening and resize. “Terapkan ke draft” persists reviewed corrections before the separate business submission. Keep the disabled Apply control mounted after success so another financial action cannot replace it under the pointer; reopening clears its transient applied message while retaining the applied draft. One short shared `ConfirmationDialog` names the selected count, exact total, atomic submission and reviewed Material stock effect: valid selected rows are submitted together, remaining rows stay draft, submitted rows retain their result and cash remains unpaid. Discarding the remainder or replacing unapplied local changes with the server version also uses shared confirmation. `ExpenseBatchActionCard` keeps verification, approval/rejection and payment as separate immutable human decisions with concise stage titles. One row uses `ProposalInlineReview` inside the card, foregrounding labeled before/after status and applicable account-balance comparisons with readable previous snapshots. Nominal, required reason, account, bank reference and receipt remain visible, while supporting requester, quantity, unit-price and budget facts live in the existing plain Rincian disclosure. Multiple rows retain the same grouped sheet and five-row pagination, with one active static “Rincian” row and no selection or inline editing. Each row keeps its identity, category, nominal and reviewed status effect readable; the payment bank reference and receipt link stay visible before supporting detail. Sheet account identification belongs with the protected summary, keeping its label intact while long values wrap. Stage budget detail stays in a plain disclosure below the reviewed collection at every width. Embedded blockers follow project identity before facts; sheet feedback retains its grouped surface; every stage has its own short shared `ConfirmationDialog` repeating the reviewed effect and totals. Reuse divided `FactRow` and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values. Owned proof, current permissions/project scope, validation, streaming, pending, stale/expired and conflict gates guard each action; feedback retains recovery beside its message. Saved receipts name the completed stage and lead to project expenses; preparing the next stage requests a fresh preview without running it. This family extends Atria’s cool canvas, Manrope, white grouped owners and shared focus, dismissal, sizing and motion without new tokens or another behavior owner.

rules.name: The AI Finance Input Review Rule
rules.body: AI proposals for a client invoice, project invoice schedule or company budget defaults reuse `FinanceInputProposalCard` and the deterministic Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. A single invoice exposes project identity, invoice number, exact amount, translated stage, due date and notes directly in the owning `ProposalCardShell`, with one explicit “Buat invoice” action. Invoice schedules retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal: desktop puts complete immutable termin rows in shared `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` in the main pane, with concise grouped summary facts and protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads the summary before rows and keeps actions in the bottom footer. Paginate five termin rows at every width and preserve the current page and review owner through resize and reopening. Up to three changed company default values show every labeled before/after comparison inline; larger default changes retain the dedicated shared review. Both default paths require one short shared `ConfirmationDialog` repeating the company identity, effect and reviewed summary. Preserve untouched settings and state that changed defaults apply only to future setup, without changing existing project budgets. Company default decisions require the actual `manage:budget_settings` and `view:settings` rights alongside AI access, independently of project `dataScope`; invoice and schedule decisions retain project permissions and scope. Compose complete, unwrapped rupiah values with divided, wrapping `FactRow` and `MoneyValue` using `variant="fullDynamic"`; reuse `ProposalInlineReview`, `ProposalDiffRow`, `ProposalReviewFeedback` and the existing shared controls. Place blocking feedback after entity identity and before reviewed values, with recovery attached to its message. The proposal is immutable; corrections through chat request a fresh complete preview. Ready proof, current rights, streaming, pending, stale/expired and conflict gates guard the explicit save, which sends only the stored proposal identity. Busy model generation disables actions while retaining their business labels; “Menyimpan…” appears only during a real save. Saved receipts identify an unpaid client invoice or defaults updated for the next setup and link to the project’s invoices or Settings. Invoice creation does not record a client payment or move cash. This family inherits the cool Atria canvas, Manrope, white grouped owners, capsule controls and shared focus, motion, sizing and dismissal without new tokens or another overlay owner.

rules.name: The AI Operational Settings Review Rule
rules.body: AI approval-threshold and expense-category proposals extend `FinanceInputProposalCard` and the deterministic Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. Partial threshold patches show at most two complete labeled before/after rupiah comparisons inline in the owning `ProposalCardShell`, preserve omitted values and require one short shared `ConfirmationDialog` repeating company identity, reviewed changes, effect and the supplied human reason. Owner approval applies from the actual Settings threshold (nominal >= threshold); zero means all eligible related submissions need Owner review. Changed thresholds apply only to future submissions; existing submissions retain their frozen decisions and over-budget safeguards remain. Category patches with at most three actual comparisons expose every change inline; metadata/status corrections save directly, while a supplied ratio patch requires protected confirmation. More than three comparisons retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal: desktop puts grouped comparisons in the main pane and concise facts/protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads summary facts before comparisons and keeps actions in the bottom footer. Reuse `ProposalInlineReview`, `ProposalDiffRow`, `GroupedSurface`, divided `FactRow` and adaptive `SheetFooterActions`. Long prose uses the existing stacked comparison on desktop and vertical comparison on mobile; short fact labels stay intact while values wrap. Shared `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` keeps complete rupiah values unwrapped and preserves exact sen when present. Read actual Settings with `view:settings`; threshold mutations require `manage:approval_settings`, category mutations require `manage:expense_categories`, and ratio patches additionally require `manage:budget_settings`, alongside AI access and independently of project `dataScope`. Keep the five canonical category identities/codes intact and active. Ratio effects distinguish a reference-only correction from synchronized changes to the current authoritative active default allocation and category reference; other defaults, existing project budgets and recorded transaction amounts stay intact. Keep the mandatory human reason and effect readable before commit. Corrections through chat request a fresh immutable preview. Place `ProposalReviewFeedback` after identity and before values, retaining recovery with its message. Ready server proof, current rights, source access, streaming, pending, stale/expired and error gates protect saving; revoked access blocks the decision, changed sources require a fresh proposal, and pending work prevents repeat submission and dismissal. Explicit save sends only stored proposal identity. Busy model generation retains business action labels; “Menyimpan…” appears only during a real save. Saved receipts name the completed Settings change and lead to “Buka pengaturan”. Preserve proposal, page and overlay ownership through resize and reopening. This family inherits Atria Operate’s cool canvas, Manrope, white grouped owners, capsule controls and shared focus, sizing, dismissal and motion, without new tokens, selection checkboxes, inline editors or another overlay owner.

rules.name: The AI Vendor Payment Review Rule
rules.body: AI vendor scheduling, approval, rejection and payment remain separate human decisions in `VendorPaymentWorkflowCard`. Every stage uses a complete inline `ProposalCardShell` with readable bill/vendor identity, project, exact nominal, payment date and supplied account facts. Scheduling also exposes the amount not yet scheduled and the current approval requirement; approval/rejection exposes the labeled before/after decision and the supplied human reason; payment exposes the bank reference and before/after account balance and remaining bill amount. Compose flat, divided wrapping `FactRow` values and readable `ProposalDiffRow` snapshots through `ProposalInlineReview`, with `MoneyValue` using `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values. Only permission-supplied category allocation and realization support goes into the shared plain “Rincian” disclosure. Scheduling uses the explicit “Simpan jadwal pembayaran” action directly; approval, rejection and payment require one short shared `ConfirmationDialog` repeating bill/vendor identity, supplied facts and the reviewed effect. Rejection retains critical action/confirmation semantics. Keep embedded `ProposalReviewFeedback` after identity and before reviewed values, with recovery attached to its message. Corrections through chat request a fresh immutable preview. Ready server proof, current action/source permissions, streaming, pending, stale/expired and error states guard saving; pending work prevents repeat submission and confirmation dismissal, and the commit sends only stored proposal identity. The visible effect and saved receipt distinguish schedule/decision from cash recording: scheduling or approval/rejection keeps cash and stock unchanged; payment records Atria’s cash/ledger effect without sending a bank transfer, while stock stays unchanged. Saved receipts keep stage-specific outcomes and lead to the project’s vendor-payment context. This family inherits Atria’s cool canvas, Manrope, white grouped owner, capsule controls and shared disclosure, focus, sizing, dismissal and motion without new tokens or another overlay owner.

rules.name: The Saved RAB Workflow Review Rule
rules.body: AI proposals for existing RAB Draft corrections, linked-source refreshes, client bundles, initial approval, revisions and Change Order decisions keep project/RAB identity, revision, concise status, reviewed-part count and the client selling total after the action in a compact `ProposalCardShell`, with an action chosen by the Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. Small single-row Draft corrections expose complete before/after client fields in the chat card and save directly. Linked-source refresh exposes only client-safe quantity, unit and selling-price differences, preserving client labels, descriptions, visibility and bundle prices. A refresh affecting at most one row and three changed fields uses the inline decision; larger refreshes retain the shared sheet. Client confirmation, Change Order rejection and approval without budget risk use the card plus one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`; line exclusion remains protected. Bundles, baseline revisions, multiple rows, larger patches and budget risk retain a wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal, `desktopAsideSummary` and `desktopFooterPlacement="aside"` keeps contextual `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` rows in the left pane, concise selling/contract facts and protected actions in the right aside, and one summary-first column with bottom actions on mobile. Reuse the incumbent Manrope roles, cool canvas, white grouped owners, capsule controls and shared focus, dismissal, motion and viewport sizing. Retained sheets paginate five reviewed parts at every width; inline rows use embedded `ReviewCollection` inside the chat card. Pagination, open details and controlled financial disclosure state stay with the same owner through resize and reopening. Each row shows readable identity, action, unit/quantity context and applicable client subtotal before details. Changed client fields and business status use labeled `ProposalDiffRow` comparisons, two columns on desktop and one column on mobile. Shared “Rincian” / “Ringkas” controls reveal static client fields without selection or inline editing. Keep supplied revision reasons and Change Order scope summaries in left-aligned, wrapping prose; client confirmation shows the human-supplied date and evidence/reference. Bundle review names the members and the client package price; totals use the package price without counting its member rows again, and dissolution names their return to individual client rows. Contract, internal-cap and category-allocation impacts appear only for a proposal carrying those effects and a reader with budget-view permission. Keep the resulting contract and internal cap as divided `FactRow` values in the summary; a plain “Rincian dampak budget” disclosure within the card or below retained-sheet rows compares contract, cap and all category allocations, identifies preserved manual allocations and shows actual spend unchanged. Any new allocation below actual spend remains visible outside the disclosure as an icon, concise verdict, category name and exact shortfall, and is repeated in the approval confirmation. Reuse wrapping fact labels and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values. The proposal is immutable; corrections through chat request a fresh proposal. Action permissions, streaming, pending, stale and expired states guard confirmation; changed data offers a fresh proposal and pending work prevents repeat submission or dismissal. Only an explicit action sends the stored proposal identity. Approval, client confirmation, bundle dissolution, revision cancellation, Change Order rejection and line exclusion require one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`, from the card or retained sheet, retaining the reviewed selling total and permitted financial consequences; an emergency override states its explicit reason. Saved results use the action-specific completed outcome and next step, then “Buka RAB proyek”, while retaining stock/cash status. Revisions preserve the approved baseline until the formal approval decision. Draft corrections, bundles and Change Order preparation do not change project budget; reviewed approval may update contract and budget allocations without moving stock or cash. Internal cost, margin, vendor/private notes stay outside client content, and client publication remains manual. This family extends shared review primitives without introducing tokens or another overlay owner.

rules.name: The RAB Export Workbench Rule
rules.body: Manual RAB export and the AI `RabExportCard` share the same `RabExportDrawer`. The chat card leads with the selected project, client, RAB title, revision, readable Draft/Disetujui status, visible offer-row count and exact client selling total before “Preview & unduh”. Compose these facts through `ProposalCardShell`, divided `FactRow`, `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` and decimal-aware `fractionDigits`, plus shared adaptive `SheetFooterActions`. The wide, content-sized `FormSheet` preserves its owner and local presentation preferences: desktop keeps paper preview or grouped customization in the main pane, with revision/total, the shared `AdaptiveSelect` format choice and protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads identity and summary before `SegmentedTabs`, preview/customization and bottom actions. PDF, Excel (.xlsx) and Gambar (.png) require an explicit download action. “Tampilan dokumen” opens grouped styling fields; its primary action returns to preview before downloading. Formatting is a local human preference, with receiver overrides scoped to the document identity and a client-name default; receiver labels never imply approval. Keep current permissions, owned source checks, expiry and changed-source feedback authoritative. A failed source read or denied access removes the paper and financial facts, with recovery beside the message. Recheck the source before creation and before releasing a chat download; pending work blocks repeat download and dismissal. This read-only flow does not require a business approval dialog. It inherits Atria's Manrope, cool surfaces, capsule controls and shared focus, sizing, dismissal and motion, without new primitives or tokens.

rules.name: The Client Paper Rule
rules.body: RAB preview and exported documents retain the established white-paper aesthetic with fixed print colors independent of the app theme. Human-selected document accent, studio identity/logo, title, agreed payment terms and preparer/receiver presentation belong to this client artifact, not the workspace palette. The edited document title carries into PDF, XLSX and PNG; exact selling amounts retain their decimal precision. Client-facing paper shows visible offer rows and package selling prices without counting bundle members again, and excludes internal RAP costs, margins and private vendor notes. `RabExportCanvas` keeps zoom and fit controls in normal flow above the paper, using shared labeled `IconButton` and `Button` controls with mobile/coarse-pointer touch targets and compact desktop density. The focusable preview supports arrow keys, Page Up/Down and Home/End alongside pointer pan and pinch zoom; motion uses the existing snappy preset and becomes immediate for dragging or reduced motion. Paginated PDF continuation pages repeat document identity and table headings, keep total/payment/signature content together when it fits, and show page numbering. Preserve legibility and client context across formats without promoting print-specific type sizes, raster settings or pagination measurements into application tokens.

rules.name: The Grouped Review Collection Rule
rules.body: Use the public `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` for AI review families: Material Master, planned RAP, saved RAP changes, Tukang/Subcon package planning, RAP readiness/finalization, RAP lifecycle, client RAB drafts, saved RAB workflow changes, project stock, vendor invoice, warehouse, expense-batch drafts/decisions and staff/role administration. This shared composition is justified by persistent inline editors and contextual decisions that the sortable table contract cannot represent. `ReviewCollection` owns one white `GroupedSurface` with an accessible list, divided rows and an optional footer; use `embedded` when a grouped owner already exists. `ReviewItem` leads with readable identity/meta and an optional primary amount on the right on desktop. Mobile places supporting summary context and the complete primary amount together beneath identity, keeping the amount unwrapped and aligned to the right. Empty child content adds no detail spacing. Editable Edit / Ringkas and read-only Rincian / Ringkas share one start-aligned contextual action row after the visible summary and comparisons, directly before revealed fields; neither shares the identity or primary amount header. These supporting controls use the shared `Button variant="quiet"`: `surface-container-low`, `on-surface` and `shadow-control` through both native and scoped HeroUI desktop adapters. This explicit quiet treatment keeps row utilities subordinate to the sheet’s primary commit actions even inside white owners. Label quantity, unit, buffer and price support rather than relying on columns. Keep one inline editor active at a time; compose its shared fields through embedded `FormSection`, using `contentClassName` for the inner desktop grid rather than feature-local form infrastructure. Inline review editor labels use sentence case and the support type role above regular-weight Manrope values; numeric values retain tabular digits and mobile inputs retain the editable-text floor. The private shared `ContentReveal` preserves editor DOM and state through collapse/resize, makes collapsed content inert and hidden from assistive technology, and reuses existing disclosure height coordination, easing and reduced-motion behavior. Material Master, RAB and expense inclusion use the existing `ChoiceRow` review presentation: a stable-width Pilih/Dipilih control beside Edit in the contextual action row, with no reserved leading checkbox column. Its accessible name identifies the item and its checkbox state remains explicit on desktop and mobile. Ordinary ChoiceRow/radio presentations retain their defaults; labels, focus, touch targets and motion stay shared. Selection and status remain distinct. Immutable changes, packages and decision batches acquire no fake selection or editing. Five-row pagination applies at every width. Material corrections cache unapplied edits across rows and batch them through the existing metadata patch before the separate business save. Material checkbox and select-all/clear changes update immediately while selection metadata autosaves through one serialized queue. Keep browsing and selection usable during synchronization; only business Save, field corrections, reference creation and discard wait for acknowledgement. Coalesce rapid choices and preserve the latest intent over older responses. Failed autosaves retain visible choices, show an explicit retry, read the latest owned revision before retrying and keep business Save blocked until acknowledgement. Closing/reopening the review retains pending selection in the same card owner; local unacknowledged choices are never represented as saved business records. Material Master uses bounded content height on desktop and retains its maximum-height mobile batch composition. Keep the same `FormSheet` / `WorkflowFormSheet` owner, concise desktop summary/protected actions in the right aside, financial details below reviewed rows in the main column, and mobile summary order. Preserve natural viewport-bounded sizing, dirty/conflict and Apply/Save separation, destructive/finalization confirmations, client privacy and idempotent saved receipts. Page tables remain HeroUI; no new overlay, selection, money, focus or touch-target primitive accompanies this review composition.

rules.name: The Readable Comparison Rule
rules.body: Reuse `ProposalDiffRow` inside the single owning `ProposalCardShell` surface. Keep the default inline layout for short before/after pairs; use `layout="stacked"` for long names, specifications, or notes. The stacked row places the field label above two columns explicitly labeled “Sebelum” and “Sesudah”, preserving line breaks and wrapping long values within each column. Use the optional `layout="vertical"` for narrow table cells such as subtotal comparisons: the field label remains above “Sebelum” and “Sesudah”, with the labeled values arranged in one column. The default inline and two-column stacked layouts keep their existing behavior. Rows remain flat with shared dividers; the proposed value uses stronger type weight rather than another card or surface.

rules.name: The Adaptive Proposal Review Rule
rules.body: For AI project and budget decisions (`PROJECT_MANAGEMENT`), staff/role administration (`ADMINISTRATION`), catalog settings, project stock, procurement/warehouse, RAP readiness/finalization, RAP lifecycle, saved RAP changes, Tukang/Subcon package planning and saved RAB workflow, `proposal-review-flow.ts` deterministically derives review and confirmation from validated actions, affected rows, changed fields, source links and budget consequences. The model cannot choose a UI path or bypass protection. Small single-record metadata, value or status changes show complete labeled before/after values inside the owning `ProposalCardShell`, with one explicit action naming the saved outcome. Small sensitive bank, valuation, physical stock, deletion, finalization or financial-approval decisions use that card plus one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. Multiple rows, larger patches, full templates/component sets, baseline revisions, complex budget effects and edit/selection/import workflows retain the shared `FormSheet`; only sensitive actions add a confirmation dialog. Every path exposes all reviewed changes and mandatory human reasons, costs, quantities and sources before commit. Secondary context expands through plain `FormDisclosure` within the same owner. Feature-level `ProposalInlineReview` composes shared `ProposalDiffRow`, divided `FactRow`, `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` and existing row renderers; use embedded `ReviewCollection` and `ProposalReviewFeedback` inside the card, without nested surface shadows. Keep mobile as the single-column source of truth and preserve proposal, page, disclosure, editor and overlay ownership through resize; width never changes the policy. Direct/protected actions use contextual “Simpan”, “Aktifkan”, “Nonaktifkan”, “Ajukan”, “Setujui” or “Tolak” labels; “Buka review” opens retained sheets. Server-owned proof, current permissions/scoping, source access, validation, streaming, pending, stale/expired and conflict gates remain authoritative on every path, with explicit human approval, recovery, repeat-submit protection and saved receipts. Existing direct Material Master single/material metadata, planned RAP and client RAB draft edit/selection reviews, and legacy finance/role flows retain their established behavior.

rules.name: The Own Profile Proposal Rule
rules.body: AI own-profile name and photo add/replace/remove proposals use one compact `OwnProfileCard` in `ProposalCardShell`, led by the actual session user's identity and “Akun Anda sendiri”. Show every changed name as a labeled `ProposalInlineReview` before/after comparison, with two columns on desktop and vertical values on mobile. Photo changes compare shared square `UserAvatar` previews (64px) labeled “Sebelum” and “Sesudah”; retain the same centered cover crop as the saved avatar. Keep small quiet “Lihat foto” buttons separate from the avatar with an accessible label identifying the side, and let the shared `MediaPreviewDialog` own full-image inspection, focus and dismissal. Removal shows the shared initials fallback and explicit removal copy. Show the source filename and explain that the selected private chat image becomes a profile copy only after Save; the original chat attachment stays private. The avatar copy is cropped only during that explicit save. Use adaptive `SheetFooterActions` with quiet “Koreksi lewat chat” before primary “Simpan profil”; the pair shares a row when labels fit and wraps otherwise. This reversible own-profile change saves directly from the complete card. Corrections request a fresh immutable proposal, and the save sends only its stored identity. Server proof, current access, streaming, checking, pending and errors guard the action; changed or expired proposals offer “Minta usulan terbaru”, while inspection failures retain “Periksa lagi”. Access denial hides cached identity, comparisons and photos while keeping blocker/recovery visible. A no-op states that no save is needed and leads to “Buka profil saya”. Saved cards retain the recorded before/after result and current verified identity; a later profile change uses neutral `InlineStateRow` history copy explaining that the comparison records the earlier save. Keep that historical notice distinct from blocking stale, expired or access failures. Shared icon-button tooltips remain non-interactive annotations: Escape and Tab continue to the owning dialog's dismissal and focus trap, including React Aria event continuation. Reuse `Button`/`ButtonLink`, shared avatar crop, focus, touch targets and media ownership within Atria's Manrope, cool canvas, white grouped owner and capsule controls; this rule adds no tokens or overlay infrastructure.

rules.name: The AI Quick Start Proposal Rule
rules.body: AI setup progress, initial-stock decisions and first-project proposals use the immutable `QUICK_START` family through `QuickStartCard` and `ProposalCardShell`. Compact progress cards expose complete labeled current/next comparisons and actual setup facts through `ProposalInlineReview`, with vertical values on mobile. Pause/resume retain the stored stage without skipping review; retry names the current attempt without implying repeated business writes. Initial-stock decisions add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog` repeating the decision and its readiness-only effect; stock and cash remain unchanged. First-project creation retains one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal: desktop keeps identity, project facts and category rows in the main pane and concise financial summary/actions in the right aside; mobile reads summary before category rows and keeps actions in the bottom footer. Keep “Nilai proyek”, “RAB disetujui” and “Budget internal” visible. Supporting default, target margin and any unallocated amount expand through one plain “Rincian budget” `FormDisclosure`, inside the mobile summary or a white `GroupedSurface` below category rows in the desktop main column. Disclosure content uses its shared 16px inner padding with flat divided `FactRow` values. Review every category through `ReviewCollection` / `ReviewItem`, five rows per page at every width, with readable ratio context and `MoneyValue` using `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped amounts and exact sen when present. The retained review uses primary-first adaptive `SheetFooterActions`: ink “Buat proyek pertama” and white quiet “Koreksi lewat chat”, stacked in the desktop aside and paired or wrapped on mobile. Corrections request a fresh preview; server proof, current permissions/source access, checking, streaming, pending, stale/expired and error gates protect the explicit identity-only save. Pending work prevents repeat submission and dismissal; no-op decisions say no save is needed. Preserve proposal, page, disclosure and overlay ownership through resize and reopening, using shared focus, reduced motion and dismissal. Saved project review says the Draft project and category budget are recorded, Quick Start is complete, and leads to “Buka proyek”; it does not imply a created RAB document, expense, stock movement or cash transaction. This family inherits Atria Operate’s Manrope, cool canvas, white grouped owners and capsule controls without new tokens or primitives.

rules.name: The Administration Review Rule
rules.body: AI staff name, role and status changes, role details/project scope, and unused-role deletion use the immutable `ADMINISTRATION` family through `AdministrationProposalCard`. Show readable staff/peran identity and permitted email, exact labeled before/after values, added or removed access, affected people and session consequences, and the human reason before an explicit commit. A compact single-row diff stays in `ProposalCardShell` with shared `ProposalDiffRow` and divided `FactRow`; multiple people or larger changes retain a wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with `ReviewCollection` / `ReviewItem`, five rows per page at every width. Desktop keeps reviewed rows in the main pane and concise `GroupedSurface` summary/actions in the right aside; mobile reads summary before rows with adaptive `SheetFooterActions` below. Prior values remain readable snapshots with `strikeBefore={false}`; long values use labeled stacked desktop or vertical mobile comparisons. The validated input determines protection: staff role/status, role project-scope and deletion changes add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`; name/detail-only changes use the explicit direct save. A model-supplied sensitivity flag cannot choose confirmation. Keep the same proposal, pagination, sheet and confirmation owners through resize. Corrections request a fresh preview through chat; stale/expired, streaming, permission, source and pending gates block commit, with contextual recovery and repeat-submit protection. Source-read or commit denial suppresses cached identity, email, diffs, reason and consequences in the card, sheet and confirmation while retaining the blocker/recovery. Saved results lead to canonical Settings. This family inherits existing Manrope, cool neutral grouped surfaces, quiet capsules and shared focus/dismissal/motion; no token or primitive is added. Evidence: [review composition](apps/web/features/ai-chat/components/proposal-cards/administration-proposal-card.tsx#L150-L440), [source/commit gates](apps/web/features/ai-chat/components/proposal-cards/administration-proposal-card.tsx#L67-L128), and [adaptive policy](apps/web/features/ai-chat/utils/proposal-review-flow.ts#L78-L88).

rules.name: The Project Stock Review Rule
rules.body: AI project-stock reservation, usage, return, release and waste proposals reuse `ProjectStockProposalCard` and keep project/action identity, material count and the explicit stock/noncash consequence in a compact `ProposalCardShell`, with an action chosen by the Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. A single material exposes its complete stock comparison and mandatory quantity, cost source and human note in the chat card: reservation and release save directly; use, return and waste add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. Release and waste overlays use the concise titles “Lepas reservasi” and “Material terbuang”. Multiple materials retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal: desktop keeps contextual rows in the left pane and concise summary/protected actions in the right aside; mobile keeps the summary before rows and actions in the bottom footer. Retained sheets reuse `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` with five-row pagination at every width; inline rows use the same collection embedded in the card. Retain page, open details and budget disclosure state through resize. Each immutable row shows material, location, unit, quantity, source and the human note. Visible comparisons show only changed stock metrics; reservation/use/release/waste foreground physical stock, available stock and related reservation, while return foregrounds physical stock, available stock and related net usage. Static “Rincian” / “Ringkas” reveals all five before/after states: physical, total reserved, available, related reservation and related net usage, alongside stock unit cost and its source. Use shared `ProposalDiffRow` with `strikeBefore={false}` so valid previous quantities remain readable snapshots; other comparisons retain the default strike-through behavior. Budget facts appear only with budget-view permission. Lead the grouped summary with an icon and concise verdict, then Material allocation, realization after the action, any noncash delta and any over-allocation including pending review. A plain budget disclosure below rows carries RAP, previous realization, pending review and remaining budget. Reuse wrapping `FactRow` labels and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values. Reservation holds project quota while physical stock, realization and cash stay unchanged; release makes only this project’s reservation quota available again, with physical stock, Material realization and cash unchanged. Waste names the audit reason, reduces physical stock and uses this project’s reservation first; its Material realization follows the recorded cost source without cash movement. Use/return may change Material realization according to the recorded cost source, without cash movement, and return does not automatically add reservation. Corrections through chat request a fresh immutable proposal; stale/expired or unauthorized states block saving. Keep `ProposalReviewFeedback` after project identity and before rows, with recovery beside its message. Only use, return and waste require the shared `ConfirmationDialog`, naming the reviewed material or batch and permitted financial consequences; reservation and release use an explicit direct action from the card or retained sheet. Pending work blocks repeated submission and dismissal. Saved results retain static details and lead to “Buka stok material” at the canonical `/materials` route. This family reuses the incumbent Manrope, cool canvas, white grouped owners, quiet capsules and shared overlay/motion infrastructure without adding tokens or another behavior owner.

rules.name: The Procurement and Warehouse Review Rule
rules.body: AI vendor-invoice, receipt-cancellation, warehouse-transfer, stock-count and direct stock-correction proposals reuse `ProcurementWarehouseProposalCard` and keep actual source identity, the reviewed action and its explicit cash/stock consequence in a compact `ProposalCardShell`, with an action chosen by the Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. Request, submission and rejection status decisions remain in the chat card with their complete reason and reviewed effect. Small vendor-bill drafts save directly; bill submission and physical stock changes add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. Receipt-cancellation overlays use the concise titles “Ajukan pembatalan”, “Setujui pembatalan” and “Tolak pembatalan”. Larger invoice or warehouse row sets retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal, keeping immutable contextual `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` rows in the desktop left pane and concise summary/protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads the summary before rows, with actions in the bottom footer. Retained sheets paginate five rows at every width; inline rows reuse embedded `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem`. Retain page, open details and budget disclosure state through resize and reopening. Invoice identity includes vendor, project, category, bill number, amount and due date; invoice lines retain their supplied name, quantity, unit, amount and source. Keep source evidence readable without fabricating a single Material/RAP link for a multi-material invoice. Warehouse rows identify material, location, unit and the reviewed quantity or count. Labeled `ProposalDiffRow` comparisons use static before/after snapshots with `strikeBefore={false}`; previous stock values remain valid evidence. Direct stock corrections (`STOCK_CORRECT`) show physical and available stock with explicit units, plus the supplied delta and unchanged reservation. The common audit reason is left-aligned wrapping prose under “Alasan koreksi” in the inline review, sheet summary and confirmation; retained rows show a distinct “Alasan untuk material ini” note without repeating the common reason. A single material reviews inline plus one short confirmation; batches use the existing white divided rows, five-row pagination, desktop main/aside panels and mobile summary/list stack. Shared quiet “Rincian” / “Ringkas” controls sit at the row end, after visible summary and comparisons, and reveal static source and consequence facts without selection or inline editing. Reuse wrapping `FactRow` labels and complete, unwrapped `MoneyValue` amounts with `variant="fullDynamic"`. The concise outcome label is “Hasil”, leaving long outcome copy to wrap in its value. The grouped summary leads with an icon and concise verdict; current budget-view permission controls both budget detail and the over-allocation fact. A plain “Rincian budget” disclosure stays below reviewed rows. Current action permissions and source access govern review and confirmation; stale or expired data blocks saving and offers a fresh preview. Corrections through chat request a fresh immutable proposal. Keep `ProposalReviewFeedback` after context and before rows, with recovery beside its message on desktop and below it on mobile. Only bill submission, nominal corrections of stored vendor bills, warehouse transfer, direct stock correction, stock-count approval and receipt-cancellation approval open one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`, repeating identity, effect and permitted summary. Draft saves and request, submission or rejection status decisions use an explicit direct action. Either path sends only the stored proposal identity. Pending work blocks repeat submission and dismissal. Copy distinguishes saving a vendor-bill draft from recording an unpaid bill, and states that payment remains a separate action. Receipt cancellation identifies the original receipt and supplied reason before its stock consequences. A request leaves stock unchanged and awaits another user’s decision; independent approval cancels the whole receipt with an audited stock correction while vendor bills and cash stay unchanged; rejection records its reason and keeps the receipt and stock intact. Transfer states that stock moves between locations while reservations and cash stay unchanged. Saving a count retains a draft without correcting stock; submission requests another user’s approval, approval applies the reviewed correction, and rejection retains stock with its supplied reason. Direct correction records the stock movement and audit reason while reservations, average cost, budget and cash stay unchanged. Saved receipts retain static details, action-specific completed copy and the appropriate canonical draft, expense or warehouse destination. This family inherits Manrope, cool canvases, white grouped owners and shared quiet controls, focus, dismissal, motion and sizing without adding tokens or another behavior owner.

rules.name: The Warehouse Intake and Opening Review Rule
rules.body: AI project receipts, company warehouse stock-in and opening-stock request, approval, rejection and reversal extend the Procurement and Warehouse Review Rule through `ProcurementWarehouseProposalCard`. Keep the actual source, destination, reviewed quantities, cost basis and explicit stock/cash effect readable before the human decision. Use the action-specific review titles “Review penerimaan”, “Review stok masuk”, “Review saldo awal”, “Setujui saldo awal”, “Tolak saldo awal” and “Balik saldo awal”, with concise commit and saved-outcome copy for each action. A single material row reviews inline in the owning `ProposalCardShell`; larger batches retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal, `desktopAsideSummary` and `desktopFooterPlacement="aside"`. Desktop puts immutable contextual `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` rows on the left, with concise grouped summary facts and protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads the summary first and keeps actions in the bottom footer. Paginate five rows at every width and preserve the same review owner, page, open details and budget disclosure through resize and reopening. Material rows show supplied identity, location, unit, quantity and cost context, with readable before/after stock snapshots and static “Rincian” / “Ringkas” disclosure; this family has no row selection or inline editor. Reuse `FactRow` and right-aligned `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values, including the primary material amount below row context on mobile. Keep whole “Referensi…” labels intact with `wrapLabel={false}`, allowing the source value to wrap. A missing material/location inventory pair must explicitly disclose that it will be created only on confirmation. Physical receipt, stock-in, opening approval and opening reversal require one short shared `ConfirmationDialog` from the inline card or retained sheet; after identity and effect, show exact money facts first, then material count, before status and reason so the decisive totals are initially visible. Opening requests and rejection use an explicit direct action: a request waits for another checker without changing stock; rejection retains stock and records its supplied reason. Approval posts the reviewed opening quantity and cost; reversal names the whole eligible opening balance being undone and its audit consequence. Project receipt copy distinguishes stock intake from the separate payment; company stock-in states that it has no project or payment. All saved outcomes retain the action-specific result, unchanged cash and the canonical warehouse or opening-stock destination. Current rights, source proof, stale/expired, streaming and pending gates retain the inherited protected commit, which sends only stored proposal identity; chat corrections request a fresh immutable preview. Inherit Manrope, the cool tonal canvas, white grouped owners, ink primary and contextual capsule actions; the shared `FormSheet`, `ConfirmationDialog` and `SheetFooterActions` keep white-on-gray modal hierarchy, existing footer order, focus, dismissal, sizing and motion without new tokens, primitives or another overlay owner.

rules.name: The Stored Vendor Bill Correction Rule
rules.body: Corrections to saved vendor bills extend `ProcurementWarehouseProposalCard` with the actual bill, project, vendor and category source, complete changed fields and mandatory human reason visible before commit. Use “Review tagihan” and “Simpan koreksi tagihan”. Up to two changed rows without non-Material over-allocation review inline in the owning `ProposalCardShell`; documentary changes save directly and nominal changes add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. Larger changes or non-Material over-allocation retain one content-sized `FormSheet`: immutable contextual `ReviewCollection` rows sit left on desktop, with concise grouped summary and protected actions right; mobile reads summary first and uses the bottom footer. Bill number, due date and notes expose complete before/after text; retained rows reuse divided `FactRow` pairs labeled “Sebelum” and “Sesudah” beneath field identity. Nominal `ProposalDiffRow` comparisons use readable static snapshots and do not repeat the proposed amount as the row’s primary value. Reuse unwrapped `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"`; when an unpaid bill has zero completed payments, omit duplicate “Sudah dibayar” and “Sisa tagihan” facts. Preserve fractional rupiah exactly in stored-bill reviews and confirmations through the shared `MoneyValue` optional two-decimal precision (`fractionDigits={2}` only for noninteger monetary values), keeping integer displays and the default `fractionDigits={0}` unchanged. The short monetary confirmation repeats actual identity, old/new amounts and permitted risk amounts before status and reason, and states that cash and stock stay unchanged. Budget details follow the reviewed rows in the main desktop pane and below changed fields on mobile. Reuse one separate `GroupedSurface` with an inset, plain `FormDisclosure` and aligned `FactRow` values; keep the right summary compact and avoid a raised capsule against its edges. The procurement family shares this disclosure composition and preserves its expanded state through resize and reopening. No checkboxes or inline editors are added. Current source proof, permissions and shared-writer eligibility remain authoritative: project/vendor/category/Material/RAP/package links stay fixed, paid amounts remain locked, void bills cannot change, active payment schedules block nominal corrections, and completed-payment/net-receipt floors apply. Blockers retain shared contextual recovery with disabled save; stale data requests fresh proof. Preserve review, disclosure and overlay ownership through resize. Saved outcomes name the correction and audit reason and lead to canonical `/expenses`. Inherit Manrope, the cool canvas, white grouped rows, capsule controls, ink primary and shared focus, dismissal, sizing and motion without new tokens or another behavior owner.

rules.name: The Catalog Settings Review Rule
rules.body: AI vendor creation, correction and status, library creation, correction, status and archive, complete pricing-template/component saves, inventory defaults and reasoned average-cost valuation reuse `CatalogSettingsProposalCard`. A compact `ProposalCardShell` keeps the actual entity, action and consequence readable, with an action chosen by the Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. Small single-record vendor or library corrections, status/archive decisions and inventory defaults expose complete before/after values in the chat card with an explicit direct save/action. Bank details and average-cost valuation add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. Larger patches, library creation, source/category-link changes and complete pricing-template/component saves retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal: desktop places immutable contextual rows in the left pane and the concise grouped summary/protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads the summary before rows, with actions in the bottom footer. Retained sheets reuse `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` with five-row pagination at every width; inline review composes the same shared facts and comparisons without another owning surface. Retain page and open details through resize and reopening. Library/default/valuation overlays use the concise titles “Item baru”, “Koreksi item”, “Status item”, “Arsip item”, “Default stok” and “Valuasi stok”. Reviewed vendor contact, bank and status fields remain visible inline without a disclosure. Pricing rows show labeled before/after costs, selling prices or component quantities; static “Rincian” / “Ringkas” reveals contextual source and change facts, including component additions and removals. A template save reviews the complete component set, retaining existing identities and naming omitted components as removals. Status actions preserve other stored metadata. Catalog changes affect future references; existing RAP, RAB, bills, actual spend and cash retain their recorded values. Inventory defaults review minimum stock and reference price separately from average-cost valuation. Valuation shows before/after average unit cost and stock value, with its human audit reason; physical and reserved quantities, project realization and cash stay unchanged. Reuse wrapping `FactRow` labels and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah amounts. Shared `ProposalDiffRow` uses `strikeBefore={false}` so previous values remain readable snapshots. Keep `ProposalReviewFeedback` after entity identity and before rows, with recovery attached to its message. Corrections through chat request a fresh immutable proposal. Saving requires owned server proof, current action permission and a ready proposal; stale or expired data blocks saving and offers a fresh preview. Only bank changes, average-cost valuation and template component removal require the shared `ConfirmationDialog`, repeating entity identity, effect and reviewed summary. Other catalog decisions use an explicit direct action from the card or retained sheet. Either path sends only the stored proposal identity. Pending work blocks repeated submission and dismissal. Saved results retain static detail and lead to “Buka pengaturan” at the canonical `/settings` route. This family inherits Manrope, cool canvases, white grouped owners, quiet capsules and shared focus, dismissal, sizing and motion infrastructure without adding tokens or another behavior owner.

rules.name: The Project and Budget Decision Review Rule
rules.body: AI project metadata corrections, client-reference changes, Project Manager assignment, activation, closing, category reallocation and budget submission, approval or rejection reuse `ProjectManagementProposalCard`. Its compact `ProposalCardShell` leads with project identity, the proposed action and readable status; retained-sheet entries keep the contextual action or changed-category count beside “Buka review”.
