Inline paths expose complete reviewed differences, authoritative blockers and permitted financial warnings in the card; retained paths expose them in the owning review before approval. The Adaptive Proposal Review Rule derives the path from validated input: metadata patches of up to three fields without a client-reference change and budget submission use an explicit direct action. Client-reference changes, Project Manager assignment, activation, closing, reallocation, budget approval and rejection add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog`. Metadata patches larger than three fields and reallocations affecting more than two categories retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet`; sensitive decisions retain their confirmation there. Desktop uses `desktopAsideSummary` and `desktopFooterPlacement="aside"`: identity, reviewed rows, human reasons and financial detail belong in the main left pane, with concise grouped summary facts and protected actions in the right aside. Mobile reads the same context and summary in one column, with protected bottom actions. Shared `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` render immutable contextual rows with five-row pagination at every width; static “Rincian” / “Ringkas” reveals supplied supporting facts without selection or inline editing. Preserve page, open row, budget disclosure and overlay ownership through resize and reopening. Reuse `ProposalInlineReview`, labeled `ProposalDiffRow` comparisons with `strikeBefore={false}`, divided wrapping `FactRow` values and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah amounts. Reallocation shows each changed category’s before/after allocation, identifies how many categories change and retains the other category allocations; larger reviews keep the full category context in the collection. A plain “Rincian budget” disclosure exposes secondary financial facts within the same review owner. Current action permissions, the applicable budget or profitability grant and the absence of a review error govern financial facts, category amounts and warnings; a failed access or refresh must not leave those values visible. Activation names each authoritative readiness result with an icon and concise status. Server-returned readiness and closing blockers remain the saving barrier and appear through `ProposalReviewFeedback` after project identity and before reviewed values, with recovery attached to its message. Human reallocation and rejection reasons and the closing note use left-aligned, wrapping prose in the main review, inline card and applicable confirmation, rather than compressed summary values. The proposal is immutable: corrections through chat request a fresh proposal from current sources. Streaming, current permissions, readiness, pending, stale and expired states guard explicit confirmation; pending work prevents repeat submission and dismissal, and changed data offers a fresh proposal. Either path sends only the stored proposal identity. The short confirmation repeats project identity, reviewed effect, supplied reason or note and permitted financial consequences before its action. Saved receipts retain the action-specific completed outcome, including the final profitability snapshot for closing, keep the stock/cash status visible and lead to “Buka proyek” on the canonical project route. This family inherits Atria’s Manrope roles, cool canvas, white grouped owners, capsule controls and shared focus, dismissal, sizing and motion without new tokens or another visual world.

rules.name: The AI Bank and Cash Review Rule
rules.body: AI account creation, metadata/theme correction, activation/deactivation, company cash inflow/outflow and recorded inter-account transfer reuse `BankCashProposalCard` and the deterministic Adaptive Proposal Review Rule. Small decisions expose complete account identity, supplied facts and readable before/after values inline in the owning `ProposalCardShell`. More than three metadata comparisons retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal: desktop places `ReviewCollection` / `ReviewItem` changes in the main pane and concise changed-field/stored-balance facts plus protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads those same summary facts before changed fields and keeps actions in the bottom footer. Bank, account-number or holder changes, nonzero opening balance, cash movement and transfer add one short shared `ConfirmationDialog` repeating account identity and the reviewed effect. Cash confirmations lead with nominal, date and reference, followed by source/destination facts, before account-balance comparisons. Plain metadata/theme/status changes and zero-balance account creation retain an explicit direct save. Reuse divided, wrapping `FactRow`, `ProposalDiffRow` with `strikeBefore={false}` and shared `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values. Shared adaptive `SheetFooterActions` keeps quiet correction before primary commit inline, primary-first stacked actions in desktop review asides and adaptive mobile pairs; confirmations reuse the adaptive shared action layout and standard primary tone. Corrections through chat request a fresh immutable preview. Account-read permission and source denial govern identity, facts and comparisons; blocked feedback stays after identity and before values, with recovery attached to its message. Current action rights, ready server proof, streaming, pending, stale/expired and error guards protect saving; a pending save prevents repeat submission and dismissal, and only explicit human approval sends the stored proposal identity. Model previews remain read-only. Saved receipts name the completed account/cash action and lead to “Buka rekening dan kas”. Deactivation retains stored balance/history; cash entry records company cash in Atria, and transfer records both account effects while total cash stays unchanged. Recording never sends a transfer to the bank. The family inherits Atria’s cool canvas, Manrope, white grouped owners, quiet capsules and shared focus, sizing, dismissal and motion without new tokens or another overlay owner.

rules.name: The AI Bank Reconciliation Review Rule
rules.body: AI bank-statement import, matching and exception marking/clearing reuse `ReconciliationWorkflowCard`, with actual account identity and the reviewed effect in the owning `ProposalCardShell`. Multirow imports and matches retain one wide, content-sized `FormSheet` with preserved dismissal: desktop keeps contextual `ReviewCollection` and `ReviewItem` rows in the main pane and concise grouped summary facts with protected actions in the right aside; mobile reads the same summary before rows and keeps actions in the bottom footer. A single mutation or exception decision stays inline. Paginate five rows at every width and retain page, selection, candidate choice, editor and overlay ownership through resize and reopening. Each mutation shows its description, date, translated direction, complete nominal and source, duplicate status or chosen Atria record. Reuse the contextual `ChoiceRow` review inclusion beside shared quiet Edit / Ringkas controls, without a leading checkbox column. Keep one shared inline editor open at a time; import corrections use embedded `FormSection` and the existing date, direction, text and money controls, with explicit “Terapkan koreksi” separate from business confirmation. Matching uses the shared selector for readable candidate dates, references and exception context; ambiguous candidates require an explicit choice. Selection and candidate choices update immediately and persist without replacing the review with a loading skeleton; business confirmation waits for acknowledgement and completed corrections. Summaries separate selected incoming and outgoing totals and show duplicate count for import or remaining unselected count for matching. Reuse divided, wrapping `FactRow` and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped rupiah values. Every save requires one short shared `ConfirmationDialog` with flat reviewed facts inside its existing owner, rather than another nested summary surface. Exception cards and confirmations show the nominal once, readable before/after status and the supplied human reason. Shared adaptive `SheetFooterActions` keeps quiet correction before commit inline, primary-first stacked desktop aside actions and adaptive mobile pairs. Account/source denial hides unavailable facts; recovery stays with `ProposalReviewFeedback` after account identity and before reviewed values. Current permissions, owned-source proof, draft revision, streaming, pending, stale/expired and conflict barriers guard explicit approval and prevent repeated saves or pending dismissal. Saved receipts identify the selected import/match outcome or changed exception status and lead to “Buka rekonsiliasi”. Import stores bank mutations for later matching; matching pairs existing records; exception decisions update reviewed status without creating cash, moving balances or changing stock. This family inherits Atria’s cool canvas, Manrope, white grouped owners and shared quiet controls, focus, dismissal, sizing and motion without new tokens or another overlay owner.

rules.name: The Shared Table Header Rule
rules.body: Page desktop tables retain HeroUI primary-table grammar: `surface-container-low` cohesive outer frame, header and footer, `on-surface-variant` column labels, white body rows and native table geometry. Keep sorting, hover/selection, disabled treatment, keyboard focus, cell density and supplied domain order intact. AI chat Markdown tables retain the same desktop page-table header tone and their existing mobile header treatment. This table grammar applies to deliberate tabular workflows; modal reviews follow the shared grouped-review contract and have no blanket HeroUI table requirement. Mobile review collections keep white divided grouped rows. Express table and surface separation through existing semantic tokens.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is the only hue in the system. Warning and critical are the same family at different intensity, not different colors. Healthy, completed, pending, and inactive states stay neutral ink/gray with icon and copy carrying the meaning — never assign a fourth or fifth "status color."

rules.name: The No-Warm-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Neutral surfaces never take on cream, beige, brown, red, or yellow undertones. A neutral is always drawn from the cool ink/gray/canvas family above, never approximated with a warm gray utility because it "looks close."

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every monetary value uses tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) so digits never shift width as they change. Primary values stay on one line at 320–430px; when a full amount is too long, show a compact primary value with an exact secondary value alongside, never a wrapped primary.

rules.name: The One Role Rule
rules.body: Pick the semantic type role whose purpose matches, not the one whose pixel size happens to look close. An arbitrary size remains valid only for something with no role in this table.

rules.name: The Editable Text Rule
rules.body: On viewports below 1024px or devices with a coarse pointer, editable text inputs and textareas have a 16px minimum (`--text-input-min`). The shared stylesheet raises small type roles on the control itself, including grouped forms, money/quantity controls, search, chat, and HEX entry. Larger text keeps its size; labels, helper copy, read-only facts, and fine-pointer desktop controls keep their compact roles. Keep manual pinch zoom available.

rules.name: The Nested-Stays-Flat Rule
rules.body: A surface that sits inside another owner, or that is deliberately recessed, carries no lift: inset metric cells, icon tiles, metric pills, grouped form rows, and segmented-tab tracks. Elevation marks what owns hierarchy, so applying it to a nested element destroys the signal.

rules.name: The Lift-Is-Not-Loud Rule
rules.body: The resting lift must stay imperceptible element-by-element. If a shadow is legible on its own, it belongs to floating chrome (`raised`/`floating`/`sheet`/`overlay`), not to a resting surface — and if a static card reaches for `shadow-floating`, the role is wrong, not the value.

rules.name: The Selection-Stays-Flat Rule
rules.body: Selection and searchable-selection dialogs use one compact inset white option group with shared dividers. A selected row keeps the same white surface and is identified by a terracotta label plus check, never by another nested owner card or full-row tint.

rules.name: The Desktop Selection Interaction Rule
rules.body: Shared desktop plain, search and filter selectors can open an empty collection to show truthful empty guidance, while existing search, custom-value entry and explicit create actions remain available. Intentional options with an empty value, such as Tidak ditautkan, remain valid choices rather than being treated as no options. Dependent features may explicitly disable a selector for an unavailable prerequisite, with visible project/budget or recovery guidance; existing pending and permission guards remain authoritative. Public Button and IconButton forward the caller ref to the actual button DOM node in both mobile and desktop presentations, including tooltip-wrapped icon controls, so the shared HeroUI anchored owner controls positioning, outside dismissal and focus restoration. Selection updates the existing draft callback; business mutation keeps its explicit action. Create/menu handoffs use the shared exit queue, category/project confirmations retain their existing workflow owner, and nested selects/menus inherit the active sheet layer and shared focus/dismissal coordination. Escape closes the top surface while preserving the parent draft; feature code adds no portal or focus owner.

rules.name: The Field-Association Rule
rules.body: FormField owns one stable label/control/message relationship. Shared controls inherit its generated ID, required state, invalid state, and helper or error description unless an explicit caller value is supplied. Read-only facts and choice groups use their own row or fieldset semantics instead of an orphaned label.

rules.name: The Declared-Dismissal Rule
rules.body: Every editable form sheet declares whether close discards ephemeral input, confirms local dirty state, preserves parent or draft state, or delegates to an existing managed Save Draft / Discard / Continue flow. Backdrop, Escape, pull or header close, and programmatic close follow the same policy path.

rules.name: The One-Overlay-Owner Rule
rules.body: Calendar, media preview, selection, search, confirmation, and morph-detail wrappers use the internal DialogFrame for focus, visual viewport, body lock, Escape, reduced motion, and layering. Raw DialogFrame never crosses into feature code. Shared sheet chrome owns the opt-in desktop aside: `desktopAsideSummary` scrolls in a padded region above protected footer actions. The invisible aside reserves 256px for 224px content with 16px shadow gutters, preserving header/body alignment. Intrinsic summary and action heights determine natural sizing and viewport caps; feature code supplies content without a nested scroll owner, and bottom-footer behavior remains the default. At desktop widths, the viewport host centers the relative sheet using its actual animated height throughout expansion, collapse and reversal. Never derive its top offset from the target height. At disclosure animation start, shared infrastructure measures the final intrinsic layout height and restores temporary measurement styles before paint. Desktop sheet height and disclosure reveal both use `transitionEaseSmooth` so they settle together, without chasing intermediate resize frames. Non-disclosure size changes and sheet entrance/exit retain `transitionSpringSmooth`; mobile sheets keep their existing motion path and absolute bottom anchoring. The private shared controller owns this coordination; feature consumers do not duplicate it.

rules.name: The Stable Workspace Rule
rules.body: Providers, route children, draft/selection state and portal owners stay mounted across resize. Layout changes without navigation or a new session. A focused control or open overlay retains its control presentation until the interaction ends, so resize does not replace its DOM, focus owner or dismissal policy.

rules.name: Read-only pull dismissal
rules.body: DetailSheet may opt into dismissOnPull for short introductions such as Panduan Peran. On mobile a downward pull from natural height uses the same onClose path as X, backdrop and Escape; expanded sheets first collapse. Non-resizable handles support keyboard close. Default sheets retain resize-only gestures.

rules.name: The Disclosure Motion Rule
rules.body: Accordion and disclosure headers, including every `FormDisclosure` variant, keep native button semantics and never scale on press or tap. Expansion retains the chevron rotation and content height/opacity reveal through the shared motion presets. Disclosure spacing belongs to padding inside the animated clipped content and collapses with it. Reduced motion makes the reveal and chevron change immediate. Ordinary action `Button` and `IconButton` controls, including navigation and edit actions, retain their existing press-scale behavior.

rules.name: The AI Desktop Form Panel Rule
rules.body: Material Master review, single/batch correction and reference creation, plus assistant preferences, use the shared wide, content-sized `FormSheet` layout on desktop. `OperationalFormSheet` and `WorkflowFormSheet` forward the existing desktop size, footer placement and aside summary slots without changing their default behavior. The left column owns fields or reviewed rows; the right aside owns concise draft readiness/reference counts or selected preference facts and protected actions. Shared `SheetFooterActions` stacks full-width action buttons in desktop asides while retaining its two-button mobile footer and accessible disabled-reason guards. Material counts and blockers move to the aside only on desktop; mobile retains its established single-column summary/blocker sequence and bottom actions. Reuse `GroupedSurface`, divided `FactRow` values and the existing aside shadow gutters, sizing, focus, dismissal and motion coordinator. Keep draft/selection/editor state above responsive changes, five-row Material pagination, metadata correction separate from business Save, and reference creation separate from material creation. Preferences retain permission-filtered focus options, dirty dismissal, Save and Reset. Compact rename and destructive confirmations remain focused decision dialogs; the composer wizard remains in the composer.

rules.name: The AI Review Feedback Rule
rules.body: Blocking and validation feedback in adaptive chat-card reviews and retained review sheets belongs after entity/project identity and before reviewed values or rows. Compose the feature-level `ProposalReviewFeedback` from shared `GroupedSurface`, `InlineStateRow` and `Button`; preserve the exact server message, a concise heading and a semantic status icon. Use its `embedded` presentation inside `ProposalCardShell` so the existing card remains the sole surface and shadow owner; retained sheets keep the grouped feedback surface. Keep any recovery control with its message: trailing in the wide desktop content row, below the description on mobile through the optional shared `InlineStateRow actionPlacement` contract. The default trailing placement remains unchanged for other consumers. Use the shared quiet compact button so recovery stays subordinate to the business decision. The chat-card action area, retained-sheet desktop aside and mobile protected footer contain commit/correction controls and ordinary state guidance, without loose error text or a detached retry after them. Field-specific validation remains next to its fields, permissions and confirmation barriers remain authoritative, and the existing Material Master selection/analysis feedback flow retains its domain context. Status changes reuse the existing card or sheet sizing and motion owner; no new surface, motion, focus or touch-target primitive is introduced.

rules.name: The Budget Summary Inspection Rule
rules.body: Budget summary inspections use the existing proposal family: project identity and a compact matching/differing verdict precede up to three actual labeled before/after differences in `ProposalCardShell`; a contextual detail action opens the full inspection. Clean results have no synchronization action, while critical or over-budget conditions remain visible even when summaries match. Optional read-only `FormSheet` detail uses one grouped `ReviewCollection`/`ReviewItem`, at most five category rows per page and one open detail; desktop keeps summary/actions in the shared aside, while mobile stacks summary above rows and uses bottom actions. Preserve page, disclosure and overlay state through resize and reopening. Reuse `ProposalInlineReview`/`ProposalDiffRow`, divided `FactRow` and `MoneyValue` with `variant="fullDynamic"` for complete, unwrapped amounts. Explicit synchronization opens shared `ConfirmationDialog` naming project, changed categories and actual changed fields; a pending, paid or status-only correction must not imply changed consumption. Keep stale/expired, access and uncertain-outcome feedback beside its recovery action. The saved verdict distinguishes a recorded sync from a freshly verified persisted result; synchronization updates derived usage only, without implying changes to cash, stock, contract, cap or allocations. No new visual tokens or overlay owner are introduced.

rules.name: The AI Activity Outcome Rule
rules.body: AI activity uses shared `FormDisclosure` with `variant="activity"`: one compact contextual summary, no extra surface, and details opened by the reader. The summary reflects the current task outcome, with running work, unresolved failures and stopped work taking priority over waiting or completion. A recovered read remains in the flat semantic history as a neutral refresh icon with visible “Pulih”; it is not a current failure. Recovery requires a later genuine result from the same tool with the same canonical inputs within the same assistant message, preserving target, filters and page. The bounded historical exception is a one-character project-search validation failure followed by a scoped project list whose actual results supply the subsequent project-selector options. A different tool or target, access denial, mutation, interruption, missing result or structured output error cannot establish recovery. Expanded unresolved steps show fixed, safe category guidance without raw inputs, values or error strings. Waiting follows the active input request and its current wizard values: an unselected required project shows “Pilih proyek untuk melanjutkan”; a valid project selection shows “Menunggu isian Anda”. Submitted, cancelled or dismissed requests stop waiting while recovered history remains. Details keep small shared `ActivityMark` / `AppIcon` state icons, accessible completion text and visible running, failed, recovered and stopped labels without elevation or repeated completion badges. Waiting uses a static clock; only running activity loops, using unified motion presets with reduced-motion and visibility support. Within one assistant turn, render the model-written public introduction first, one stable activity disclosure second, then final answer bubbles, complete domain cards and follow-up suggestions. Persist the introduction as a separate data part, not answer text or another assistant message. It describes a future step without financial results or a claim of saving. Before model copy arrives, the same compact disclosure shows honest pending status; actual tools, errors and waiting states update it in place without changing its surface, focus or expansion. Preserve supplied introductions after completion and refresh; legacy and direct fast answers do not acquire fabricated preambles. Introduction-only or unfinished background-read replies retain retry recovery. Final answer bubbles complement selected result cards. Server-verified cash and budget sections may carry typed card narratives; use a short alternative only when its exact source call has a matching, valid, displayed card. Company cash details and per-account amounts stay in the card; named account/bank questions retain their scoped conclusion. Budget copy preserves paid/pending facts, requested qualifications and category rows omitted by the shared card-selection policy. Invalid, absent, hidden or unsupported cards retain the complete canonical answer, and partial errors remain visible. Model-generated card answers use concise supported takeaways without copying lists or before/after rows. Legacy history is not heuristically rewritten; stored presentation metadata restores the same complementary view. Transcript scrolling treats initial/history alignment separately from streamed persistence IDs. New responses follow only until the newest user question reaches the reading inset; incidental scroll/resize events never promote that cap to bottom following. Upward reader gestures cancel queued movement. Deliberate return to the bottom or the newest-answer control can resume bottom following. Idle disclosure/card growth updates the control visibility without moving the reading position; reader interaction cancels bounded opening alignment.

rules.name: The Manual Desktop Form Panel Rule
rules.body: Meaningful manual input and review sheets use the existing wide, content-sized FormSheet with desktopFooterPlacement="aside" and desktopAsideSummary. The main pane owns editable fields and reviewed rows; the right pane owns live draft context and protected existing actions. Reuse OperationalFormSheet, WorkflowFormSheet, GroupedSurface and SheetFooterActions. Narrow aside facts use FactRow layout="stacked" so labels and long values remain readable; its default inline contract stays unchanged. Monetary summaries retain exact cents through shared MoneyValue formatting when present. Existing input → review → commit, pending/disabled guards, HTML form associations, dirty dismissal and presence remain with their owners. Unknown references and unread/failed sources never become healthy zeros. Short names/reasons, profile/security decisions, confirmations and read-only details stay focused; dedicated desktop page editors retain their layout. Mobile/native-pinned composition, footer ordering and draft/focus state through resize remain. No feature introduces its own modal, portal, scroll owner or finance/material calculation.

rules.name: The Settings Desktop Workspace Rule
rules.body: Settings inherits Dashboard's compact white panels, semantic typography, native HeroUI tables and existing capsule controls. Finansial compares the budget cap and allocation defaults in one quiet band, followed by a category allocation table with formula/simulation context and the approval thresholds. State the applicability to new budgets or requests beside the settings rather than implying changes to recorded projects. Katalog uses complete Material and Item & Price Library tables with inline search/filters and controlled 10/25/50 pagination; Lokasi shows only supplied reference facts. Organisasi uses Tim, Vendor and Peran tables with actual contact, status, scope, user and permission data, preserving password requirements, Owner/system-role locks and existing editors. Kesiapan places required and optional foundations in independently sized grouped panels with real status and action links; its initial-stock subflow retains the explicit existing decisions. Structural skeletons follow the active tab, source failures stay distinct from valid empty or zero data, and controls use the documented type roles. Domain owners retain filtering, full-result sorting, selection, pending work and drafts; presentation does not change permissions, scope or mutation rules. Library editing uses one OperationalFormSheet at every width, with the existing desktop main/aside contract and mobile bottom-sheet composition, keeping dirty fields and nested overlay ownership through resize. Mobile and native-pinned hierarchy remains the source of truth.

rules.name: The Expenses Desktop Workspace Rule
rules.body: Standalone `/expenses` inherits Dashboard and Settings' compact Atria grammar. A source-backed comparison band, peer/status views and inline search/filter controls precede native HeroUI tables. At 1024–1279px rows open a list/detail progression with a back action; from 1280px the table and independently sized detail panel sit beside each other only when an actual row supplies context. Empty and filtered-zero claims, bills and payments use the full table width without reserving an aside. Native active-row highlighting follows visible context: from 1280px it identifies the row shown in the right detail panel; the narrower list has no fallback-selected row while that panel is hidden. Preserve explicit selection through resize and clear it only through existing Back/filter interactions. Vendor detail actions use two columns when the owning panel reaches 512px and one column in the narrow aside; a guarded single action fills the row. Field expenses expose only supplied project/requester/category/date/nominal/status and evidence facts, while vendor bills and payments preserve the existing payment-summary calculations and distinguish scheduling, approval and cash recording. Reuse public DesktopTable, controlled DesktopTablePagination, SegmentedTabs, GroupedSurface.desktopPanel, MoneyValue, SearchInput/FilterSelect, status, facts and shared overlays. Domain owners filter and sort the complete authorized collection before 10/25/50 pagination and retain truthful totals; exact values preserve supplied cents. Assigned field costs remain the actor's own requests, assigned vendor records follow PM projects, and account identities remain redacted without bank-view permission. Tabs and create/verify/pay entry points follow domain rights rather than role names. Compact draft recovery distinguishes waiting, failure/retry and a valid empty result. Selection, filters, pending work and recovery stay above responsive presenters; focused controls and existing sheets retain their single focus/dismissal/confirmation owner through resize. Structural skeletons match claims, bills and payment collections without fabricated zero totals or focusable placeholders. Mobile and native-pinned composition remains authoritative; the project-embedded desktop continuation is documented below. This adaptation introduces no backend write path, database migration, finance formula, bulk action or real-time claim.

rules.name: The Approvals Desktop Workspace Rule
rules.body: Canonical `/approvals` extends the Dashboard and Expenses grammar with a compact queue-count/value/priority/waiting band, peer views, inline search/project/priority filters and a native HeroUI table. The six columns preserve supplied request/project identity, readable type, requester, nominal, queue date and priority reason; initial priority order follows the source-ranked queue. Reuse public DesktopTable, useDesktopTable and controlled DesktopTablePagination to filter and sort the complete authorized collection before 10/25/50 pagination, retain truthful totals, reset the page after filter/sort/page-size changes and clamp it after source shrink. Fixed-layout columns use the shared widthPercent contract rather than feature-local table geometry. At 1024–1279px the first row action opens detail and Back clears explicit selection; from 1280px the table sits beside an independently sized 288px contextual aside. Start with no selected row or detail panel. Native single selection opens detail only after explicit pointer or keyboard activation; activating the selected row again clears selection and closes detail. Empty selection and empty or filtered-zero queues use the full table width. The public DesktopTable onRowSelectionChange callback reports a row or null through HeroUI/React Aria; existing row-action consumers retain their action behavior. Pending decision guards block selection changes, and explicit selection survives resize. Detail groups supplied facts, exact amounts, evidence and actual budget/stock consequences before the existing guarded decision actions. Inventory purchase value contributes no additional project actual when the source marks it as inventory; opening stock explains physical stock/audit effects separately from cash, vendor debt and project actual. Shared MoneyValue retains supplied cents in rows, detail and confirmation. Queue visibility and finance-row access follow existing domain permissions and scope; decision controls additionally require the matching cost or opening-stock approval right. Read-only access stays explicit. Rejection, opening-stock and emergency self-approval reasons, pending guards, confirmation, evidence inspection and mutation callbacks remain with the existing owner. Incoming source refreshes wait while a decision is open or pending, and acknowledged decisions stay absent during a lagging refresh. Keep route children, selection, filters, table state and overlay ownership stable through resize. Pending Change Orders remain a compact plain FormDisclosure linking to the existing project RAB workflow. Structural loading mirrors summary, controls, ten table rows, pagination and contextual detail with inert/hidden placeholders and truthful busy copy. Mobile and native-pinned composition remains authoritative. This extension adds no write path, finance formula, bulk decision or automatic payment.

rules.name: The Materials Desktop Workspace Rule
rules.body: Canonical `/materials` extends the accepted Dashboard, Expenses, Approvals and Reconciliation grammar with compact receiving/project-stock/warehouse actions, one divided stock-value/available-value/location-risk/uncovered-RAP band and Ringkasan / Inventori / Kebutuhan / Aktivitas peer views. Overview separates a bounded five-material attention preview, pending decisions and three recent events from the complete collections. Each recent event is a keyboard-focusable shared ghost Button opening its exact existing activity detail. Inventory filters locations before invoking the canonical grouped-stock summary; physical, reserved, available, minimum and value facts therefore describe the selected locations. A worst-location status beside an aggregate quantity names the affected count as “N dari M lokasi” when multiple locations are present. Needs retain project/RAP identity, actual item units and supplied quantities; their estimate describes the whole RAP row, separate from debt or payment, and available stock is not automatically allocated. Never add quantities across unlike units. Reuse public DesktopTable fixed widthPercent columns, desktopTablePage, controlled DesktopTablePagination, SegmentedTabs, GroupedSurface.desktopPanel, SearchInput/FilterSelect, MoneyValue, status, FactRow, PageState and existing outer sheets. Filter and sort the complete authorized inventory/needs collections before 10/25/50 pagination; the four activity collections use bounded API reads with server-side filtering, counts, sorting and pagination, separate from mobile preview caps. Keep each collection’s controls and page in URL state with truthful totals, page resets and clamping. At 1024–1279px the first row action opens detail and Back clears explicit selection; from 1280px an actual row supplies an independently sized 18rem contextual aside. Native active-row highlighting follows visible context only; empty and filtered-zero results use the full width. Detail preserves supplied cents and per-item units before the existing explicit receiving, stock, receipt-reversal or count workflow. Restricted/unavailable RAP sources stay distinct from valid empty or fulfilled needs, and pending activity totals come from the complete scoped summary. Existing inventory/domain permissions, tenant and assigned-project fences govern initial, paged and exact-detail reads. The stable MaterialsControlCenter retains drafts, selection, pending state and single overlay ownership through resize; source refresh waits while an overlay or pending workflow is active and stale activity reads are ignored. Structural loading mirrors the active tab, compact band, controls, table, pagination and optional context with inert/hidden placeholders and truthful busy copy. Mobile and native-pinned composition remains authoritative. This extension adds read contracts and scoped reads without changing writers, money movement or material projection formulas.

rules.name: The Projects Desktop Workspace Rule
rules.body:
Canonical `/projects` extends the accepted Atria Operate grammar with a compact title/create action, one divided active-project band for project value, internal budget, consumed budget and remaining budget, peer views and inline search/client/PM/status/health filters. A six-column native HeroUI table compares project identity, value, budget, consumed, remaining and condition. Filter and sort the complete authorized collection before controlled 10/25/50 pagination; retain truthful filtered totals, deterministic ties, page resets and clamping. Keep portfolio controls in prefixed URL state while preserving unrelated parameters and the hash. A missing budget stays distinct from a valid zero; show supplied paid, pending and projected-margin facts only with their canonical source metadata. Compact values and exact detail use shared MoneyValue and retain supplied cents. At 1024–1279px a first row action opens detail and Back clears explicit selection; from 1280px an actual row supplies an independently sized 18rem context panel. Native highlight identifies visible context only, with no fallback-selected row behind a hidden panel. Empty and filtered-zero results use the full width.

The project's Ringkasan/Budget surface at `/projects/[id]?tab=overview` keeps a compact identity header and peer navigation above the four financial facts, paid/pending/usage/margin context and a five-category comparison table. Category context exposes exact allocations, consumed, paid, pending and remaining amounts before permission-supplied existing actions. Header and budget verdict share canonical effective health, including the stored risk floor; missing, restricted and unavailable sources remain neutral and distinct from healthy zero. Reuse public DesktopTable, desktopTablePage, DesktopTablePagination, SegmentedTabs, FilterSelect, GroupedSurface.desktopPanel, MoneyValue, status, FactRow, PageState and existing shared FormSheet owners. The stable list/detail workflow owners defer incoming source updates while a workflow is open or pending and retain drafts, selection, focused controls and overlay ownership through resize. Structural skeletons mirror the compact portfolio or overview hierarchy with inert, hidden placeholders and truthful busy copy. This extension preserves mobile/native composition, RAP/RAB special views and other detail tabs/editors; it adds no finance formula, bulk workflow or automatic mutation.

rules.name: The Project Planning Desktop Workspace Rule
rules.body: The project's RAP and RAB views extend the accepted Projects/Dashboard grammar on canonical routes at >=1024px. RAP leads with internal execution cost, Material/Tukang/Subcon context and the existing setup or review stages; RAB leads with the client selling value, actual approved baseline, revision and document visibility. Keep internal planning and client document facts distinct. Use compact white owning panels, divided comparison bands, inline controls and native HeroUI tables through public DesktopTable, desktopTablePage, controlled DesktopTablePagination, SegmentedTabs, GroupedSurface.desktopPanel, SearchInput/FilterSelect, MoneyValue, status and FactRow primitives. Filter and sort each complete authorized collection before 10/25/50 pagination; retain truthful totals, deterministic ties, page resets and clamping. Separate prefixed URL state preserves each collection's controls, unrelated parameters and the hash. RAB starts in stored document order; changing table sort never changes export order. Bundle-member visibility reflects its own visibility and its parent bundle; client totals use the bundle price without counting members again. RAP's purchase summary counts material records needing purchase, never sums quantities across unlike units; row quantities retain the existing source projection and their unit. Use supplied values and exact cents through shared MoneyValue, without inventing margin or baseline facts. At 1024–1279px the first row action opens detail and Back clears explicit selection; from 1280px an actual row supplies an independently sized 18rem context panel. Native highlight identifies visible context only, with no fallback selection behind hidden detail; empty and filtered-zero collections use full width. Existing material, package, source, bundle, revision, Change Order, approval, override and export owners retain their drafts, selection, focus, dismissal and pending guards through resize. Defer incoming source data while any owning workflow is open or pending, then reconcile source identities against the accepted revision after it closes. Existing action permissions remain independent; desktop presentation grants no write capability. Structural route and local loading mirror the active planning hierarchy with inert, hidden placeholders and truthful busy copy. Mobile and native-pinned composition remains authoritative. This scoped extension changes neither finance/material calculations nor writer behavior and introduces no visual token family or overlay primitive.

rules.name: The Project Operations Desktop Workspace Rule
rules.body:
The project's Stok and Pengeluaran views extend the accepted Atria Operate grammar at >=1024px: compact white owning panels, divided source-backed comparison bands, peer filters and native HeroUI tables before independent record context and existing actions. Stock summaries count material records; each quantity retains its own unit. Keep project coverage, warehouse availability and recorded movements distinct: warehouse stock is not automatically reserved, and movement history is not a cash ledger. The inventory-only projection supplies material quantities without exposing internal RAP cost. Ready, missing, restricted and unavailable sources retain distinct copy; unknown data never becomes healthy zero. Embedded expenses reuse the existing claims, vendor-bill and payment workspaces within the current project, omitting redundant project columns and selectors while retaining source-backed money, status, approval and cash distinctions. Reuse public DesktopTable, desktopTablePage, controlled DesktopTablePagination, SegmentedTabs, SearchInput/FilterSelect, GroupedSurface.desktopPanel, MoneyValue, FactRow, status and existing shared workflows; add no token family or overlay primitive.

Filter and sort each complete authorized stock or expense collection before 10/25/50 pagination. Stock uses `stock-view`, `stock-materials-` and `stock-activity-`; embedded expenses use `project-${id}-expenses-view`, `project-${id}-expenses-filter`, `project-${id}-expenses-claims-` and `project-${id}-expenses-vendor-`, with separate `bills-` and `payments-` table keys inside the vendor namespace. Preserve unrelated query parameters and the hash. At 1024–1279px the first row action opens detail and Back clears explicit selection; from 1280px actual row context supplies an independently sized 18rem panel. Empty and filtered-zero results use full width; hidden detail creates no fallback highlight. Stable owners retain selection, drafts, pending protection, focused controls and shared overlay ownership through resize, deferring incoming project data while workflows are open or pending. Project-route expense and vendor forms lock project context; foreign recovery drafts remain intact with explicit guidance, and mismatched autosave/manual save/copy cannot silently move them into the current project. Structural stock/claims/bills/payment skeletons follow the active collection with inert placeholders and truthful busy copy. Mobile and native-pinned presentation retains its existing composition, with the stock summary corrected to record counts and unit guidance. Domain permissions, explicit mutation workflows and calculations remain authoritative.

rules.name: The Project Payments Desktop Workspace Rule
rules.body: The project's Pembayaran view extends Atria Operate at >=1024px with one divided band for active invoices, actual cash received, outstanding receivables and unbilled contract value, followed by Invoice/Penerimaan peers, inline filters, native tables and independent exact record context. Invoice commitment and received cash remain distinct. Canceled invoices leave active billing and debt totals while their historical receipts remain received cash. Presentation-only overdue attention uses the Jakarta calendar date before today and preserves paid/canceled status. Translate stage and status codes at the presentation boundary. Reuse public DesktopTable, desktopTablePage, controlled DesktopTablePagination, SegmentedTabs, SearchInput/FilterSelect, GroupedSurface.desktopPanel, MoneyValue, FactRow, statuses and the existing invoice, receipt and activity-detail owners; introduce no token family or overlay primitive.

rules.name: The Project Margin Desktop Workspace Rule
rules.body:
The project's Margin view extends Atria Operate at >=1024px with one white divided band for conservative projected margin, configured target margin, consumed budget and remaining budget, retaining contract value and internal-budget context. The explanation preserves the canonical projection: contract value minus the greater of consumed cost and internal budget. Target comparisons use the project's supplied target, never a fixed percentage. Five category rows compare allocation, consumed cost, remaining and readable condition before exact category context; this bounded collection needs neither search nor pagination. Reuse public DesktopTable, GroupedSurface.desktopPanel, MoneyValue, FactRow, statuses, PageState and the existing ProjectCategoryDesktopDetail. From 1280px an actual category supplies an independent 18rem context panel with native highlight; at 1024–1279px first row action opens detail and Kembali ke kategori clears explicit selection. A hidden panel creates no fallback selection. Introduce no token family, chart or overlay primitive.

Margin, actual cash and stored FINAL snapshots retain separate source contracts; missing, restricted and unavailable data remain distinct from valid zero. For a completed project with an independently authorized ready FINAL snapshot, desktop and mobile retain the frozen contract, target, consumed cost, remaining budget and cash position even when today's budget read is missing or unavailable; current category and cash-breakdown failures stay separate, while active projects and restricted margin access cannot use this fallback. Current cash uses complete exact-cents client receipts and canonical paidCost, never consumed cost; noncash stock usage does not create cash outflow. Completed projects use stored FINAL totals and cash position when supplied, with snapshot time. Category rows and received/paid cash breakdown remain explicitly current data. A missing final snapshot stays visible as unavailable history and is never manufactured from current projections. One project-keyed ProfitabilityPanel owns closing inspection, notes and shared ConfirmationDialog through resize. Closing requires view:project, update:budget, view:profitability and close:project, an active project, ready budget source, an explicit server checklist with no blockers and a trimmed note of at least 10 characters. Show read freshness and current blockers; explain that saving rechecks readiness. Failed checks or completion clear prior checklist authority. Pending guards, dirty-note discard confirmation and deferred source refresh preserve the reviewed state without carrying another project's checklist. Structural loading mirrors the summary, five-category table, optional context and cash/closing owners with inert hidden placeholders and truthful busy copy. Mobile and native-pinned presentation retain their one-column composition. Existing writer, database, authorization and finance calculations remain authoritative.

dos: Do keep exactly one accent hue (terracotta) system-wide; express urgency through its intensity (`#b84b2c` → `#97371f`), never through a new hue.

Do give every owning surface and standalone control its semantic resting lift (`shadow-surface`/`shadow-control`, or the dark-tier `shadow-primary`/`shadow-inverse`), and keep everything nested inside one flat.
Do keep every standalone interactive control a full capsule, and every container surface on the fixed 28/20/16px radius scale — never mix the two vocabularies.
Do keep primary monetary values on one line with tabular numerals at 320–430px, falling back to a compact value + exact secondary value when the full amount is too long.
Do combine status with copy and an icon/shape/position — never color alone.
Do keep motion purposeful and spring-based (`lib/utils/motion.ts` presets only) — selection, origin, continuity, feedback.
Do keep selection/search options in one compact inset white group and indicate selection with terracotta label plus the shared check glyph rather than a filled rectangle.
Do let FormField create and propagate the accessible label, control, helper, and error relationship by default.
Do declare discard, confirm, preserve, or managed dismissal behavior on every editable form sheet.
Do keep all modal focus, viewport, dismissal, reduced-motion, and layering behavior behind semantic shared wrappers.
Do put simple repeated events, transactions, and master-data rows on one grouped surface with dividers; reserve an individual card for a genuinely independent, decision-heavy entity.

Do keep every main route's `loading.tsx` a structural skeleton matching the final hierarchy (header/tabs, focal summary, expected rows, nav clearance) — never a centered spinner or generic loading card.

Do keep mobile/coarse-pointer effective touch targets at 48×48px even when the visible control is smaller; use compact shared 32–40px controls on fine-pointer desktop. Preserve keyboard focus order, screen-reader labels, safe-area clearance, and reduced-motion behavior throughout.
donts: Don't add a second or third accent color, a rainbow of category colors, or a locally-defined focus-ring color.

Don't hand-roll a shadow value or reach past the semantic role — no `shadow-[...]`, no raw `box-shadow`, and no `shadow-floating` on a static card. Never put a lift on a nested row, icon tile, metric cell, or recessed tab track, and never apply blur or glass to an ordinary surface.
Don't use glassmorphism, decorative gradients, or oversized touch chrome anywhere except a configured bank-account identity surface (the sole user-defined gradient exception).
Don't wrap a primary money value, or let a value's digits reflow without tabular numerals.

Don't add whole-page transitions, section entrances, or list-stagger animation — routes, tabs, and lists stay visually instant; only the active-pill spring and explicit local feedback (taps, sheets, disclosures) animate.
Don't warm a neutral surface with cream, beige, brown, red, or yellow undertones.

Don't ship a generic admin-dashboard or spreadsheet-like composition — a repeated formula of summary card, header pill, and identical rounded cards for every section is a tell that the content pattern wasn't chosen deliberately.

Don't use an inset metric grid for a single title/meta/value row, activity/history/transactions, or more than three equal-weight cells in one mobile row; don't give a metric cell its own shadow, elevation, or oversized radius that competes with its owning surface.

Don't nest a capsule inside another owning surface for ordinary grouped rows, or place a colored vertical severity rail or short attention marker beside an ordinary list icon — a continuous connector is timeline-only.
Don't add another owner card inside the shared option group or tint the full selected row.
Don't leave a hidden action or an ambiguous icon-only control without an accessible label, or build UI from placeholder/dummy data when real domain data exists.
